title: [P2] feat: append-only events.jsonl + JSONL transcripts (stable observability contract)
body:
**Priority:** P2 — the enabler for any rich UI; additive only
**Lane:** `lib/status.mjs` + `lib/agy.mjs` log framing — sequence after `--watch`, before the TUI.

## Context

Two observability gaps block a rich dashboard (and make post-run analysis annoying):

1. **No event history.** `run.json` is a snapshot; past transitions are lost — a UI can only diff polls. All transitions already funnel through `status.ticket()` / `status.pools()` (`lib/scheduler.mjs:284-297`), so an append-only log is a small change at existing call sites.
2. **Transcripts use custom framing.** `.booster/logs/<runId>/<ticketId>.log` is a JSON header line + `\n---PROMPT---\n...\n---OUTPUT---\n...\n===\n`, appended across strikes (`lib/agy.mjs:86-91`). Tailing requires a bespoke parser.

## Task

1. `.booster/logs/<runId>/events.jsonl`: append one JSON line per transition from the same call sites. Schema: `{ ts, runId, type: 'phase'|'pool'|'strike'|'report', ticket?, from?, to?, detail?, pools? }`. Append-only via `appendFileSync` (atomic enough at these sizes on POSIX).
2. Normalize per-ticket transcripts to JSONL: one record per agy invocation `{ ts, model, strike, ms, ok, kind?, error, prompt, output }` (i.e. move the existing header object's fields + the two text blocks into one JSON line). Name the file `<ticketId>.jsonl`.
3. Document both schemas in `docs/usage.md` as a stable read contract for external tools (the TUI issue consumes exactly this).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every phase transition in a scheduler test run appears in `events.jsonl` in order; test replays a run and reconstructs final state from events alone, matching `run.json`.
- [ ] Transcript files parse with `JSON.parse` per line; no `---PROMPT---` framing remains.
- [ ] Schemas documented; `npm test` green.

title: [P2] feat: full-screen node TUI dashboard reading run.json + events.jsonl
body:
**Priority:** P2 — big bet
**Lane:** new module/package; reads only the file contracts. **Depends on:** events.jsonl issue (required), `--watch` (supersedes its rendering, keep the flag).

## Context

With atomic `run.json` snapshots + `events.jsonl`, a full-screen dashboard needs zero scheduler coupling — it is purely a reader of `.booster/` files. Per project direction, this should be **Node/npm-centric** (ratatui/Rust was only a suggestion; a second toolchain would break the zero-dep npx story if it lived in the core package).

## Task

Decide and implement one of:

- **Option 1 (recommended): zero-dep ANSI TUI inside agb** (`agb tui /repo`, or auto-upgrade of `status --watch` when stdout is a TTY). Alt-screen, panes: ticket table (phase/strikes/model), pool gauges (inFlight/caps/requests), event timeline tail, selected-ticket transcript tail. Keys: ↑/↓ select ticket, enter toggle transcript pane, q quit. This data is low-frequency JSON — no framework needed; ~400 lines of ANSI + a render loop, consistent with the repo's zero-dep doctrine (`package.json` stays one runtime dep).
- **Option 2: separate optional package** (`agb-tui`) using Ink or OpenTUI, published independently so the core keeps zero deps. Choose only if Option 1's rendering burden proves real.

Either way: reader-only (never writes `.booster/`), degrades gracefully when `events.jsonl` is absent (snapshot-only mode), works while a run is live and after it finishes (post-mortem browsing).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live run renders all panes; `done` shows final report state.
- [ ] Render functions pure and unit-tested (state → string frame); no test needs a TTY.
- [ ] Core package still has exactly one runtime dependency.
